title: Move legacy Kanbus Secrets Manager secrets to SSM SecureString or retire them
description:
Requested by Ryan via the Prospectus session (2026-10-21). Standing rule: SSM Parameter Store standard SecureString for secrets and config; Secrets Manager only where a service requires it; nothing manually configured; delete nothing without Ryan's approval.

Secrets in legacy account 335163751677 that belong to Kanbus:
- kanbus/github-webhook/dev: created by infra/cloud/kanbus_cloud/cloud_stack.py (GithubWebhookSecret, generated).
- kanbus/mqtt-token-pepper/dev (last accessed Apr 3) and kanbus/mqtt-token-pepper/prod: created by cloud_stack.py and coordination_stack.py (MqttApiTokenPepper, generated).

The infra/cloud Python CDK app has no deploy job in CI (CI only synthesizes and tests it), so whatever is in 335163751677 was deployed by hand. The current product path (kanbus-api with @kanbus/cdk) does not use these secrets.

Plan:
1. Read-only, on Ryan's Mac: list CloudFormation stacks in 335163751677 that own these secrets, which functions reference them, and each secret's last accessed date.
2. If no live stack reads a secret, it is an orphan: propose retiring the owning legacy stack through CI (stack deletion removes its generated secrets) for Ryan's approval.
3. If a live stack reads it (most likely the prod pepper for MQTT token hashing): switch the CDK to an SSM SecureString parameter read with decryption. CloudFormation cannot create SecureString parameters, so the generated value needs a small custom resource; deploy only through a CI job.
4. Retire infra/cloud once nothing in it is live.

Not Kanbus (routed to owners): b0rd/mqtt-test/broker-password (B0rd infra/lib/mqtt-broker-stack.ts), amplify/github-app-token (Papyrus standard-site hosting; Amplify may genuinely need Secrets Manager), GoogleOAuthSecret963EF6DE-* (Auritus cdk/stacks/backend.py), SessionKey0FE01E29-* and sierrendipity/google-oauth (Sierrendipity infra/lib/stack.ts).

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Read-only check of 335163751677 (2026-10-21). Recommendation: migrate nothing, retire all three.
- kanbus/github-webhook/dev (stack KanbusCloudFoundation): read by GithubWebhookIngress about 25 times a day, fed by the push webhook 673694740 on AnthusAI/Kanbus to the legacy dev API. Downstream is failing: EfsWriter 771 errors in 1562 runs over 30 days, GitSync 80 of 1007, 11 messages in kanbus-sync-dlq-dev. ConsoleLambda had no invocations in 30 days, and no repo or client config references the legacy API or user pools.
- kanbus/mqtt-token-pepper/dev (KanbusCloudFoundation): its authorizer last ran 2026-09-02; the token admin API never ran in 90 days.
- kanbus/mqtt-token-pepper/prod (KanbusCoordinationProduction): last used 2026-09-22/23, no use since, no client config points at it.
Retained data on stack deletion: KanbusCloudFoundation keeps EFS fs-09fcbd58a2e2d2c98 (75 GB, the main cost), S3 kanbus-sync-dev-335163751677 (27 GB), Cognito us-east-1_mPUGMCuS6 (21 users) and the token table; its two secrets have DeletionPolicy Delete. KanbusCoordinationProduction keeps Cognito us-east-1_ytWCFJZy3 (1 user), two DynamoDB tables and the prod pepper secret (DeletionPolicy Retain, so it needs its own delete).
Proposed steps, each awaiting Ryan's approval: 1) deactivate the Kanbus repo webhook; 2) delete stack KanbusCloudFoundation; 3) delete stack KanbusCoordinationProduction and then the retained prod pepper; 4) decide keep or delete for the retained EFS, S3, Cognito and table data; 5) remove infra/cloud and its CI job.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Step 1 done 2026-10-21: webhook 673694740 on AnthusAI/Kanbus deactivated (not deleted). Retirement plan: 2) delete stack KanbusCoordinationProduction (50 resources, idle since 2026-09-23); 3) delete stack KanbusCloudFoundation (100 resources) after 24 hours of zero ingress invocations confirms nothing else feeds it; neither stack has exports or termination protection; 4) delete the retained data: EFS fs-09fcbd58a2e2d2c98 (75 GB), S3 kanbus-sync-dev-335163751677 (27 GB), Cognito us-east-1_mPUGMCuS6 (21 users) and us-east-1_ytWCFJZy3 (1 user), the three DynamoDB tables, and secret kanbus/mqtt-token-pepper/prod with the default 30-day recovery window; the synced board data is a mirror of the git repository and is recoverable from it; 5) PR removing infra/cloud, its CI job and docs, then delete the webhook. Execution: no CI role for AnthusAI/Kanbus exists in 335163751677, and creating one only for teardown would itself be manual configuration, so steps 2 to 4 are proposed as approved one-time CLI deletions from Ryan's Mac.

comments.text: Ryan approved the plan 2026-10-21. Step 2 done: stack KanbusCoordinationProduction deleted; its retained tables kanbus-coordination-leases-prod and kanbus-coordination-mqtt-tokens-prod, Cognito us-east-1_ytWCFJZy3 and secret kanbus/mqtt-token-pepper/prod remain until step 4. A 24-hour invocation check of KanbusCloudFoundation started before step 3; the infra/cloud removal PR is being drafted and will not merge before step 3.
